title: Unlocking the Hidden Potential of Digital Infrastructure in CRE
excerpt: Explore why controlling your building's digital infrastructure is key to boosting NOI and future-proofing assets.
content:
The Critical Role of Digital Infrastructure in Modern CRE

In the ever-evolving landscape of commercial real estate (CRE), one truth stands out: If you don't own your data & digital infrastructure, your vendors do. This sentiment was echoed throughout the inaugural episode of the Peak Property Performance® Podcast, where hosts Bill Douglas and Drew Hall unpacked the nuances of data control and digital infrastructure.

Bill and Drew, the masterminds behind OpticWise and authors of the Peak Property Performance book, emphasize the importance of owning and controlling the digital backbone of your property to leverage data-driven decisions. The need for this control is not merely academic; it's a strategic imperative that directly impacts a property's Net Operating Income (NOI) and its long-term viability.

"Most of the time, property owners don't own and control both," Bill highlighted, pointing to a gap that many owners overlook.

This opening discussion sets the stage for a deeper exploration into how data and digital infrastructure can transform your CRE operations.

Understanding the Vision Behind the Podcast

The podcast was birthed from Bill and Drew's extensive experience and research within the CRE market. Their findings were clear: property owners crave business intelligence but lack the necessary data control to achieve it. This disconnect is what the Peak Property Performance Podcast aims to address.

Bill shared an insight from their research: "We spend a lot of time with commercial real estate owners...and most of what we heard back is the property owners wanted business intelligence. But in reality, they don't have the data."

This lack of data ownership is a barrier to making informed, strategic decisions. By focusing on the foundational layer of digital infrastructure, Bill and Drew provide a roadmap for property owners to regain control and unlock new opportunities.

The Role of Business Intelligence in CRE

Drew Hall brings a technical depth to these discussions, demystifying the complexities of data usage in real estate. He highlights how harnessing this "flowing information" can lead to actionable insights, significantly impacting financial performance.

"The real power of harnessing all the information...is making it actionable, like how much of a financial difference it can make in commercial real estate," Drew explained.

By aligning data control with strategic objectives, property owners can not only optimize current operations but also anticipate and adapt to future challenges.

Clarifying the Non-PropTech Focus

A critical distinction made in the episode is that Peak Property Performance is not about PropTech; it's about the underlying infrastructure that supports it. Bill was clear: "PropTech is an industry in and of itself...but it has to run on a digital infrastructure."

This infrastructure is the backbone of any property, and owning it means having the tools to utilize PropTech solutions effectively. Without control over this layer, any advances made by PropTech are superficial and unsustainable.

Personal Backgrounds and Industry Insights

Drew and Bill's personal journeys into the world of CRE provide a unique lens through which they view these challenges. Drew's initial interest in chiropractic work highlights his passion for making a tangible difference, a theme that carries over into his work with OpticWise.

Bill, with a background in engineering and entrepreneurship, emphasizes the importance of technology in solving big problems. His experience spans multiple successful ventures, and his insights reflect a deep understanding of how technology can enhance real estate operations.

Key Challenges in Commercial Real Estate

The major concerns for property owners often revolve around occupancy, insurance, and utilities. Bill and Drew address these through the PPP 5C™ framework, which guides owners to Clarify, Connect, Collect, Coordinate, and Control their digital assets.

Bill elaborated, "We emphasize that if you actually own the connectivity user experience...then you have a lot more control of differentiation in the marketplace." This control directly affects occupancy rates and tenant satisfaction, leading to increased NOI.

Utility management is another area where data control can lead to significant savings. By collecting and analyzing utility data, owners can reduce expenses and improve efficiency, a straightforward yet powerful way to enhance property performance.

Actionable Takeaways for CRE Owners

The actionable takeaway from this episode is clear: begin by asking who owns and controls your data and digital infrastructure. This foundational question is the starting point for unlocking the full potential of your property.

Embrace a mindset of exploration and innovation. As Drew advised, "Don't be afraid to dig in. There's a lot of benefit to digging in." By taking ownership of your digital infrastructure, you position your property for success in an increasingly competitive landscape.

To dive deeper into these strategies, subscribe to the Peak Property Performance Podcast and explore their comprehensive guide outlined in the Peak Property Performance book.
